surface_summary: A series of murders and mysterious events surround the Foxhills estate and the return of the missing nephew Derek Fordingbridge, who is severely disfigured. Suspicion falls on various family members and acquaintances, including the Fleetwoods and a Frenchwoman, as the police investigate deaths, thefts, and disappearances. The case appears to involve blackmail, imposture, and inheritance disputes.
accepted_facts: Peter Hay, the caretaker, was found dead with suspicious wrist marks.
Nicholas Staveley was murdered on Neptune's Seat, shot through the heart.
Derek Fordingbridge, the claimant to the estate, is severely disfigured and missing fingers.
Cressida Fleetwood was found with the murder weapon and had motive related to Staveley.
inferred_conclusions: Cressida Fleetwood murdered Staveley in a fit of rage and fear.
Stanley Fleetwood was an accessory to the murder and tried to cover it up.
Mme. Laurent-Desrousseaux was the mysterious woman with the neat shoe and possibly the murderer.
mechanism_description: The crime was orchestrated by a gang including the claimant impersonating Derek Fordingbridge, Billingford, Simon Aird, and the faceless man. They aimed to secure the Foxhills estate by eliminating witnesses such as Peter Hay and Nicholas Staveley and coercing family members like Cressida. Paul Fordingbridge was involved in financial malversation and was kidnapped by the gang. The murders were premeditated to remove obstacles to the claimant's inheritance, with the final capture of the criminals resolving the case.
delivery_path: The gang planned to impersonate Derek Fordingbridge to claim the estate.
Peter Hay was murdered to silence a potential witness.
Nicholas Staveley was killed to prevent blackmail and remove a threat.
Cressida Fleetwood was kidnapped and coerced into compliance with threats.
Paul Fordingbridge was kidnapped to prevent interference and hide malversation.
The gang used deception, including stolen diaries and false evidence, to mislead investigators.
The police investigation, led by Sir Clinton Driffield, uncovered the truth and apprehended the culprits.
outcome_result: The criminal gang was captured, the impostor claimant exposed, and the estate's rightful succession secured.

false_assumption.statement: Cressida Fleetwood was the murderer of Nicholas Staveley, acting out of fear and anger.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: She was found with the murder weapon and had motive related to Staveley. Witness testimony and circumstantial evidence pointed to her presence at the crime scene.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The actual murder was committed by the gang members to secure the estate, and Cressida was coerced and innocent of the crime.

supporting_points: Her golf shoes matched footprints at the crime scene.
The murder weapon was found in her blazer pocket.
She had motive due to Staveley's blackmail attempts.
Witness Mme. Laurent-Desrousseaux testified to seeing her at the scene.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The timing of the shots and the wet clothes evidence showed she could not have fired the fatal shot.

red_herrings.description: Cressida Fleetwood was suspected of murdering Staveley due to circumstantial evidence and witness testimony.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Her presence at the crime scene, possession of the pistol, and motive.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: She was coerced and innocent; the murder was committed by the gang to secure the estate.

red_herrings.description: Mme. Laurent-Desrousseaux was suspected due to her presence at the scene and ambiguous testimony.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Footprint size matched the neat shoe prints; she had a past relationship with Staveley.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Her footprints were smaller impressions caused by walking in sand; she was not involved in the murder.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects were connected to the Foxhills estate and involved in the events surrounding the murders and disappearances, with no outsiders implicated.

discriminating_test.design: Recreate the tide and footprint conditions on the beach to verify timing of tracks and cartridge-case locations. Measure the length and depth of footprints and compare with shoe sizes and gait of suspects. Test the ejector mechanism of the pistol to confirm cartridge-case landing position.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals the impossibility of the Fleetwoods firing the fatal shot and confirms the timing and presence of the gang members at the crime scene.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The cartridge-case location and footprint timings must match the reconstructed tide and ejector mechanics, eliminating suspects who cannot fit the timeline or physical evidence.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with detailed descriptions of footprints, timings, witness testimonies, and physical evidence such as the pistol, cartridge-cases, and diary. The subtle clues about gait differences, the timing of the rain, and the stopped watch are all presented before the solution. The false solution is explicitly given and refuted, allowing attentive readers to deduce the true mechanism.
